WELL.note: Largest senior-housing REIT; RIDEA/SHOP structure captures occupancy + rate recovery directly, not just fixed rent. Flagship demand vehicle

VTR.note: #2 senior-housing REIT; large SHOP book leveraged to occupancy recovery against frozen new supply

OHI.note: Triple-net SNF/ALF landlord; high-yield, operator-credit-sensitive rather than occupancy-upside

NHI.note: Smaller diversified senior-housing/SNF REIT; conservative balance sheet, income tilt

SBRA.note: Smaller-cap SNF-heavy REIT; higher operator-credit risk, deeper value if recovery holds

SYK.note: Ortho + Mako robotic knees/hips; joint-replacement volumes scale directly with the 65+ cohort. Device anchor

ZBH.note: Pure-play hips/knees; most cohort-levered of the large ortho names, cheaper multiple than SYK

ISRG.note: da Vinci install-base monopoly; procedure mix skews to older-patient general surgery, recurring instrument razor-blade model

EW.note: TAVR near-monopoly; aortic stenosis is an age-driven disease, expanding to lower-risk/younger-old patients

PODD.note: Omnipod tubeless pump; type-2 expansion tracks aging + obesity, high recurring pod revenue

GMED.note: Spine + robotics; degenerative spine surgery is age-driven, post-NuVasive scale but competitive segment

ALC.note: Global #1 in surgical eyecare (cataract IOLs); cataract is a near-universal age-driven procedure

COO.note: CooperVision lenses + CooperSurgical; myopia/presbyopia demand, less purely geriatric

RXST.note: Light-adjustable IOL pure-play; premium cataract upgrade cycle, smaller-cap higher-beta optionality

SONVY.note: Swiss hearing-aid leader; sponsored ADR ~$15B mcap with adequate liquidity (unlike thin Demant/Amplifon). The one holdable hearing-aid vehicle. Hearing loss is squarely age-driven

CHE.note: VITAS hospice is the largest US hospice operator; end-of-life demand is demographically certain, diluted by Roto-Rooter

ADUS.note: Personal-care services pure-play; the structurally short home-care labor supply, Medicaid-funded aging-in-place

EHAB.note: Encompass spin-off; smaller, leveraged, turnaround/strategic-review optionality on the same home-health demand
